title: Provenance manifests for geospatial datasets
description:
A specification for one small JSON document, written next to one output dataset, that records what was done to produce it — completely enough that someone who was not there can re-run the operation and disagree with it. It covers the inputs and their hashes, the exact parameters, the coordinate-system decisions and the reason for each, the engine and its version, the environment that changed the answer, and the deterministic checks that ran.

A manifest records what was done; it does not certify that what was done was right, and the specification says so in its own text rather than leaving a reader to discover it.

The archive contains the specification, a normative JSON Schema, a standalone validator that needs no toolchain, a conformance suite of records that must be accepted and records that must be rejected, and a conforming producer in under a hundred lines that imports nothing from any product. The schema and the validator are independent implementations, kept in agreement by the conformance suite.

Status: draft. Field names and semantics may still change, and every narrowing of what conforms changes the version label.
